prerequisites: familiarity with the operation of modern PCs and the architecture of the Internet
the architecture and operation of computer networks

learning_outcomes.text: By the end of the course, the student will possess a basic understanding of cybersecurity principles, security models, and major cyber threats.
Furthermore, the student will be familiar with key techniques for protecting systems and networks.
The student will be able to analyze vulnerabilities and assess the risks associated with cyber threats using fundamental cybersecurity methodologies and tools.

By the end of the course, the student will be able to evaluate and devise simple security countermeasures for various application scenarios, balancing trade-offs between security requirements, performance, usability, and cost.
By the end of the course, the student will be able to effectively communicate cybersecurity issues and solutions to both technical and non-technical audiences.

By the end of the course, the student will have developed the ability to independently keep up to date with the evolution of major threats, technologies, and countermeasures in the field of cybersecurity.

syllabus_topics: Network-based attacks and techniques to protect data and resources
Symmetric encryption and block cipher modes
Security in wireless networks based on 802.11 standard
assessment_rules: Students must develop a thesis of at least 30 pages on one of the course topics, submitted via email to the professor at least 10 days before the exam session. The thesis is evaluated and a grade out of 30 is proposed; students can accept or reject this grade. If rejected, the student must supplement the thesis or write another on a new topic and resubmit at the next exam session. The grade considers content quality, technical language and expressive ability, ability to provide examples, and originality.
bibliography: W. Stallings, “Cryptography and Network Security: Principles and Practice”, 8th edition, Pearson, 2020.
W. Stallings and L. Brown, “Computer Security: Principles and Practice”, 4th edition, Pearson, 2018.
A. S. Tanenbaum, N. Feamster, D. Wetherall, "Computer Networks", 6th edition, Pearson, 2020
